title: 12 Best Pojangmacha in Euljiro, Seoul (2026)
description: The best pojangmacha street food tents in Seoul's Euljiro district — curated from Reddit reviews. Nogari alley, tteokbokki, soju tents & late-night eats.

places.name: Euljiro Nogari Alley (을지로 노가리 골목)

redditQuotes.text: Accidentally stumbled into a pojangmacha near Euljiro and had the most chaotic night of my trip. The ajumma started pouring me soju and grilling meat without me even ordering. I ended up sitting there for three hours with a group of salarymen.
Pojangmachas (little tent restaurants) are the best. Love drinking with ajusshis in them and letting the souls connect with our guards let down.

places.verdict: The single most recommended pojangmacha area in Seoul across all of Reddit. If you only visit one street food area, make it this one.

comparison.best for: Authentic outdoor drinking culture with office workers and locals
comparison.signature order: Nogari (dried young pollack) with gochujang sauce + cheap draft beer (₩3,000–₩5,000)
comparison.vibe: L-shaped alley of orange tents, plastic chairs, industrial backdrop — chaotic, loud, perfect
comparison.when to go: After 6 PM weekdays for the salaryman crowd; weekends for a mix of everyone
comparison.insider tip: The south side of Jongno 3-ga has calmer pojangmacha with fewer tourists than the main strip — head there for a more authentic vibe

places.editorialSummary: The single most recommended pojangmacha area in Seoul across all of Reddit. If you only visit one street food area, make it this one.
places.bestFor: Authentic outdoor drinking culture with office workers and locals

places.name: Manseon Hof (만선호프)

redditQuotes.text: Manseon Hof is a well-known spot in Euljiro, famous for its simple yet delicious menu, ranging from nogari to garlic chicken. You'll find it filled with people during spring and fall when the weather is optimal for drinking outside.

places.verdict: The original Nogari Alley institution — the one place every Seoul food guide mentions. Nearly 5,000 Google reviews for good reason.

comparison.best for: The definitive Euljiro nogari + beer experience — the OG of Nogari Alley
comparison.signature order: Nogari (dried pollack) with gochujang + garlic fried chicken + draft beer pitcher
comparison.insider tip: Multiple locations across Korea but the Euljiro original is the one you want. Spring and fall evenings when the weather is perfect for outdoor drinking are magic.

places.editorialSummary: The original Nogari Alley institution — the one place every Seoul food guide mentions. Nearly 5,000 Google reviews for good reason.
places.bestFor: The definitive Euljiro nogari + beer experience — the OG of Nogari Alley

places.name: Jongno 3-ga Pocha Street (종로3가 포차골목)

redditQuotes.text: Most of pojangmacha price in Seoul is same. One of recommendation place is in Jongno street. Near by Jongno 3 station. You can find it when you see.

places.verdict: The most famous pojangmacha street in Seoul — 200 meters of tent stalls stretching between exits 5 and 6. A rare remnant of old Seoul drinking culture.

comparison.best for: The most "classic" pojangmacha experience — orange tents, plastic stools, the full K-drama setup
comparison.vibe: Young locals, coworker groups, near Ikseon-dong — lively and loud after dark
comparison.insider tip: Arrive before 7 PM on weekends to snag a seat. Cash only at most tents.

places.editorialSummary: The most famous pojangmacha street in Seoul — 200 meters of tent stalls stretching between exits 5 and 6. A rare remnant of old Seoul drinking culture.
places.bestFor: The most "classic" pojangmacha experience — orange tents, plastic stools, the full K-drama setup

places.name: Gwangjang Market (광장시장)

redditQuotes.text: My favorite one is the food court at Gwangjang market. I had really good food there.

places.verdict: Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional market. Over 43,000 Google reviews. The bindaetteok and mayak gimbap are legendary.

comparison.best for: Daytime street food marathon — bindaetteok, yukhoe (raw beef), mayak gimbap, sundae
comparison.signature order: Bindaetteok (mung bean pancake, ₩4,000) + mayak gimbap ("addictive" mini rice rolls, ₩3,000) + yukhoe (Korean-style beef tartare, ₩12,000)
comparison.when to go: 10 AM – 5 PM for full experience. Some stalls close by evening. Weekday mornings are least crowded.
comparison.insider tip: Skip the first row of stalls (most touristy). Walk deeper into the market for the same food at better prices and shorter lines.

places.editorialSummary: Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional market. Over 43,000 Google reviews. The bindaetteok and mayak gimbap are legendary.
places.bestFor: Daytime street food marathon — bindaetteok, yukhoe (raw beef), mayak gimbap, sundae

places.name: Dalmaji Gwangjang BBQ (달맞이 광장 바베큐)

redditQuotes.text: Our best food experience in Seoul and Euljiro was Dalmaji Gwangjang BBQ. Located down a non-descript alley near the Euljiro station.

places.verdict: The highest-rated restaurant on this list at 4.6 stars. Hidden down a nondescript alley near Euljiro station — exactly the kind of place locals keep to themselves.

comparison.best for: Serious Korean BBQ in the heart of Euljiro — tabletop grills, quality meat, no pretension
comparison.signature order: Grilled pork belly (samgyeopsal) + soju. Let the staff grill it for you.
comparison.why it stands out: Mentioned by name in Seoul travel Facebook groups as "the best food experience in Seoul and Euljiro" — a hidden gem that hasn't been overrun yet
comparison.insider tip: Go with a group of 3-4 for the best experience. Order the set menu for variety.

places.editorialSummary: The highest-rated restaurant on this list at 4.6 stars. Hidden down a nondescript alley near Euljiro station — exactly the kind of place locals keep to themselves.
places.bestFor: Serious Korean BBQ in the heart of Euljiro — tabletop grills, quality meat, no pretension

places.name: Bogeonok (보건옥)

redditQuotes.text: There is nothing touristy about this place. The slightly smoky restaurant exudes the smell of beef, and service is no-nonsense. A good spot to immerse yourself amongst the locals.

places.verdict: A no-frills local bulgogi joint in Euljiro 4-ga's industrial backstreets. The kind of place where the smoke-filled room and beer-clanking locals are the ambiance.

comparison.best for: Authentic local bulgogi experience with zero tourist presence
comparison.signature order: Bulgogi stir-fry (beef, onions, green onions, enoki mushrooms) + beer + soju
comparison.vibe: Narrow alley, slightly smoky, two floors — feels like stepping into 1990s Seoul
comparison.insider tip: Down a narrow alley. Service is no-nonsense. This is where actual Euljiro workers eat lunch and after-work dinners.

places.editorialSummary: A no-frills local bulgogi joint in Euljiro 4-ga's industrial backstreets. The kind of place where the smoke-filled room and beer-clanking locals are the ambiance.
places.bestFor: Authentic local bulgogi experience with zero tourist presence

places.name: Jingogae (진고개)

redditQuotes.text: A solid, hearty and authentic meal. Jingogae has been around since 1963. The taste is light and you dip it into a slightly vinegary sauce. Very authentic vibe with basically no tourists.

places.verdict: Operating since 1963 — one of the oldest restaurants in the Euljiro area. The eobok jaengban (boiled sliced meat hot pot) is a Seoul institution.

comparison.best for: Heritage Korean dining — a sit-down meal with over 60 years of history
comparison.signature order: Eobok jaengban — boiled sliced meat, fresh vegetables, mandu (dumplings), and eggs in a light broth with vinegar sauce
comparison.price: ₩₩₩ — pricier than street food, but worth it for a proper heritage meal
comparison.insider tip: Closer to Chungmuro Station than Euljiro 3-ga. Almost no English spoken. Expect a very authentic vibe with basically no tourists.

places.editorialSummary: Operating since 1963 — one of the oldest restaurants in the Euljiro area. The eobok jaengban (boiled sliced meat hot pot) is a Seoul institution.
places.bestFor: Heritage Korean dining — a sit-down meal with over 60 years of history

places.name: Euljiro Brewing (을지맥옥)
places.verdict: The Euljiro craft beer scene's anchor — a gastropub that bridges old-school pocha culture with modern brewing. Great way to start or end a pojangmacha crawl.

comparison.best for: Craft beer drinkers who want a sit-down spot between pojangmacha hops
comparison.signature order: House-brewed beer flight + Korean-style pub food (anju)
comparison.vibe: Industrial-chic gastropub in a retro Euljiro building — the "Hipjiro" aesthetic at its best
comparison.insider tip: Perfect first stop before heading to the outdoor pojangmacha — warm up with a craft beer, then hit the tents for soju

places.editorialSummary: The Euljiro craft beer scene's anchor — a gastropub that bridges old-school pocha culture with modern brewing. Great way to start or end a pojangmacha crawl.
places.bestFor: Craft beer drinkers who want a sit-down spot between pojangmacha hops

places.name: Dongdaemun Dak Hanmari Alley (동대문 닭한마리 골목)

redditQuotes.text: The area originated when workers from the nearby shopping complex prepared chicken noodle soup in the alley. A whole chicken is boiled in soup and served with a special sauce — add knife-cut noodles into the remaining broth for the perfect finish.

places.verdict: An entire alley dedicated to one dish — dak hanmari (one whole chicken boiled in broth). Restaurants here have been operating for 5 to 30 years. A Seoul institution.

comparison.best for: A warming, hearty Korean chicken soup meal — especially good on cold nights
comparison.signature order: Dak hanmari (whole chicken in broth) + knife-cut noodles (kalguksu) added to the broth at the end
comparison.how it works: A whole chicken is boiled at your table. Cut pieces with scissors, dip in special sauce. Add noodles to the remaining broth for a perfect finish.
comparison.insider tip: Exit 9 of Dongdaemun Station. Multiple restaurants in the alley — they're all solid. The competition keeps quality high.

places.editorialSummary: An entire alley dedicated to one dish — dak hanmari (one whole chicken boiled in broth). Restaurants here have been operating for 5 to 30 years. A Seoul institution.
places.bestFor: A warming, hearty Korean chicken soup meal — especially good on cold nights

places.name: Hoegi Station Pajeon Alley (회기역 파전골목)
places.verdict: The pajeon (Korean pancake) + makgeolli capital of Seoul. A student favorite since the 1970s near Kyung Hee University. Especially magical on rainy days.

comparison.best for: Jeon (Korean pancakes) with traditional rice wine — the classic rainy-day Korean combo
comparison.signature order: Pajeon (green onion pancake, ₩8,000) or haemul-jeon (seafood pancake) + a kettle of makgeolli (₩5,000)
comparison.why here?: Multiple restaurants competing since the 1970s. The combination of crispy, savory jeon with slightly sweet, tangy makgeolli is one of Korea's great pairings.
comparison.insider tip: Koreans say "jeon and makgeolli on a rainy day" (비 오는 날 파전에 막걸리) — if it's raining during your visit, this is the mandatory activity.

places.editorialSummary: The pajeon (Korean pancake) + makgeolli capital of Seoul. A student favorite since the 1970s near Kyung Hee University. Especially magical on rainy days.
places.bestFor: Jeon (Korean pancakes) with traditional rice wine — the classic rainy-day Korean combo

places.name: Namdaemun Market (남대문시장)
places.verdict: Seoul's largest traditional market with nearly 28,000 Google reviews. Famous for kalguksu (knife-cut noodles), hotteok (sweet pancakes), and galchi jorim (braised cutlassfish).

comparison.best for: Affordable market food in a historic setting — kalguksu, hotteok, and braised fish
comparison.when to go: Early morning (5-6 AM) for the wholesale action. Late morning to afternoon for the food stalls.
comparison.insider tip: The galchi jorim (braised cutlassfish) alley inside the market is a local favorite that most tourists walk right past.

places.editorialSummary: Seoul's largest traditional market with nearly 28,000 Google reviews. Famous for kalguksu (knife-cut noodles), hotteok (sweet pancakes), and galchi jorim (braised cutlassfish).
places.bestFor: Affordable market food in a historic setting — kalguksu, hotteok, and braised fish

places.name: Myeongdong Night Market (명동 야시장)
places.verdict: The most tourist-friendly street food area in Seoul. Not the most authentic, but the variety is unmatched and it's incredibly convenient if you're shopping in Myeongdong.

comparison.best for: Casual street food grazing while shopping — tornado potatoes, tteokbokki, egg bread, lobster tails
comparison.signature order: Tornado potato (₩3,000), tteokbokki + sundae combo (₩4,000), egg bread (gyeranppang, ₩2,000)
comparison.honest take: More touristy than Euljiro or Jongno 3-ga. Prices are slightly higher. But the variety and atmosphere are great for a first-time Seoul visit.
comparison.when to go: 3 PM – 10 PM. Peak energy around 6-8 PM on weekends.

places.editorialSummary: The most tourist-friendly street food area in Seoul. Not the most authentic, but the variety is unmatched and it's incredibly convenient if you're shopping in Myeongdong.
